acceptanceCriteria: A retirement receipt binds the active Work Item Contract, Summary, Outcome, Events, repository, and Runtime identities.
Retirement preserves original active bytes in an immutable archive projection and never reports them as verified or completed.
An unfinished replacement requires an explicitly linked successor Work Item; a discarded already-integrated delivery cannot silently create a successor.
Malformed, foreign, stale, or duplicate retirement input writes no partial state.
CLI and human Outcome expose retired, replaced, and retained states with a concrete next action.
Replacement discovery rejects duplicate active/archive or symlink successor Contracts before any archive write.

Starting or activating a Work Item emits a read-only, repository-bound advisory listing active Work Items, linked worktrees, and persisted cleanup obligations, together with the current Work Item state and next action.

Unrelated residual branches, worktrees, or lifecycle obligations are warnings that do not force-stop start; an exact active identity or branch/worktree resource collision is classified as blocked before scaffold creation.
The same advisory is exposed by the CLI start result and MCP work_item_start result, and its schema and regression tests prove that start does not mutate or delete residual resources.

Start-entry diagnostics retain all independent blocking reasons, including exact resource conflicts and base synchronization failures, in one structured failure instead of hiding one behind an earlier return.
Retirement moves only artifacts belonging to the selected Work Item and preserves artifacts belonging to every other active Work Item byte-for-byte.

A recovery continuation may resume its own existing ahead checkout without being rejected by the ordinary primary-checkout advisory, while a new Work Item remains blocked by an exact resource collision.

The start advisory treats absent active or archive Work Item directories in a new or empty repository as an empty inventory, while preserving fail-closed behavior for other read errors and covering this boundary with a regression test.

A recovery successor may reuse only the predecessor checkout explicitly bound by its predecessorWorkItemId and recovery decision; unrelated active or archived resource owners remain exact start conflicts, with both paths covered by recovery regression tests.
goal: Remove stale active Work Items from repository readiness through a Runtime-validated retirement decision, preserve all original bytes and identities, and require a separately linked successor only when unfinished scope remains.
intent: Provide an explicit append-only retirement and replacement route for stale active Work Items whose delivery is already recorded in main or whose work is intentionally replaced, without claiming verification or deleting history.
outOfScope: existing historical record deletion or rewriting
